native_result.query: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, how does the number of monuments and axes changes with elements of symbolic capital?
native_result.HypoA: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, the number of monuments and axes increases along with symbolic capital
native_result.HypoB: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE, the social-capital variable (monument count) and the economic-capital variable (axes/celts) co-vary strongly with each other and move in the opposite direction to the one symbolic-capital variable that carries signal in this window, house size, while the other two symbolic-capital variables, hatchet-sword and dagger, show no within-window variation at all. Monument count and axes/celts rise together out of 3400 BCE, both peak in the 3200 BCE bin (Z=0.91 for monuments, Z=2.60 for axes/celts, the window maxima), and then decline together through 3000 BCE (Pearson r=0.87, Spearman 0.62; 100-year-change correlation r=0.82). House size starts at its window peak (Z=2.05) in 3400 BCE and declines monotonically to Z=-0.06 by 3100 BCE, so the expansion of monumental (social) and tool-based (economic) capital is temporally coincident with a contraction of house-scale symbolic capital (level correlation with monuments r=-0.35; no co-movement of 100-year changes, r=-0.04). Hatchet-sword is flat at Z≈-0.43 (within-window std 0.0045) and dagger is constant at Z=-0.58 (zero variance), so no co-variation with either can be detected across this span — their symbolic-capital expression is effectively static. Robustness: over the wider 3600-2800 BCE span (9 bins) the monument-axes association remains strong (r=0.75).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded time_series_data.csv (annual rows; indicator Z-columns populated only at 100-yr bins) and capital.csv (100-yr bins; German comma decimals parsed). Verified the two files agree exactly on the five 3400-3000 BCE window points (max abs diff 0.0). Extracted the inclusive 3400-3000 BCE window (5 bins: 3400,3300,3200,3100,3000 BCE). Computed Pearson and Spearman pairwise correlation matrices (n=5) and a lag-1 100-year-change Pearson matrix (n=4) over {MonumentCount (social capital), AxesCelts (economic capital), HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize (symbolic capital)}; used within-window stds to identify which indicators carry signal (Dagger std 0.000, HatchetSword 0.0045 vs MonumentCount 0.57, AxesCelts 0.94, HouseSize 0.82); added a one-line 3600-2800 BCE robustness check (n=9). Pollen/openness data not used, as it is not implicated in the question.
